parse_model._source: AppCommandInterface::parseCommand, app_command_interface.cpp:125-192; executeCommand :312-446; setFlag :450-465; script layer script.cpp:117; clauses added at the args merge (2026-08-04) come from the four sweep fragments' `unit_findings.c1_parse_model` and are anchored individually: src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:81-107 + :479 (inner_script_channel, unskippable_escape), app_command_interface.cpp:332-335/:2642-2693/:3676 (executeCommand_reentry), :2282-2285 (set_multi_pair), :443 (struct's dead registered path), :3435/:3453/:3459/:3776/:3849/:3917/:3927 (value_domains_are_per_branch), :3204-3225/:4608 + src/tools/utility.hpp:160-181 (boolean_grammars), src/tools/utility.hpp:85 + :2760/:4157-4159/:4193-4194/:4906 (map_operator_bracket)
parse_model.line_shape: COMMAND (KEY VALUE)*  -- first whitespace token is the command, remainder consumed as strict key/value pairs
parse_model.pair_extraction: std::istringstream 'while (str >> key >> value)': a trailing KEY with no VALUE is SILENTLY DROPPED (extraction fails mid-pair, loop exits)
parse_model.duplicate_keys: args is std::map<string,string> (tools/utility.hpp:85): a repeated key in one line keeps the LAST value; handlers iterating args see keys in ALPHABETICAL order, not line order

quoting.quote_char: double quote ONLY -- single quotes are ordinary characters; there is NO escape sequence
quoting.multi_word: opening quote pulls raw chars (spaces included) until the next '"' or end of line; an unclosed quote consumes to end of line without error
quoting.space_after_quote_normalization: any ' " ' (space,quote,space) has the char after the quote erased before tokenizing (parseCommand:151-155) -- a space directly after an opening/closing quote in ' " ' form disappears

parse_model.map_operator_bracket: `args[KEY]` is std::map::operator[] (stringHash_t, src/tools/utility.hpp:85), so reading an ABSENT key INSERTS an empty entry. The map a handler hands downstream is therefore NOT the set of pairs the line wrote. Two consequences: (a) any model of 'the keys of this line' must come from the tokenizer, never from handler behaviour; (b) four handlers forward the WHOLE map - dso3d (:1681, :1683, :1686), landscape (:2762, :2764), body (:4160, :4195), camera action create (:4583) - and three of them WRITE into it first: landscape sets args[W_PATH] (:2760, silently overwriting an author-written `path`), body sets `path` (:4157), rewrites `tex_ring` (:4159) and rewrites `keep_time` in place (:4193-4194), and transition MOVES a value out (:4906, leaving the entry empty). [units 1/2/4]

comments.script_layer: a line is dropped by the SCRIPT layer iff its FIRST byte is '#', 0, CR or LF (script.cpp:117; :114 until engine 2b8ec034 moved it - the annotator's line-provenance counter sits above it) - it never reaches parseCommand. An INDENTED '#' passes this filter and reaches the parser, where the comment rule (mid_line) drops it whole: the two layers agree in effect. [Until 2026-08-31 the parser had no comment rule and an indented '#' executed as an UNKNOWN COMMAND - 98 such lines in the 408 shipped scripts, each a log line per run; the `indented-comment` seed that reported them retired with the correction.]
comments.live_channels: the comment rule (mid_line) lives in parseCommand, which EVERY channel passes - script file, addScriptFirst splice, TCP, HTTP, pipe, joypad strings, the nested executeCommand calls - so a '#' outside quotes ends the command on every channel, uniformly. [Until 2026-08-31 TCP / HTTP / pipe / joypad strings got no comment stripping at all. Checked at the change: no ini command string carries '#'; HTTP's ?command= never delivers a raw '#' (URL fragment delimiter).]
comments.block_form: 'comment' / 'uncomment' commands toggle a skip state (intercepted before table lookup, executeCommand:351-355); skipped lines are logged 'this command has not been executed'
comments.inner_script_channel: A SECOND line-classification model exists, one layer under the script file: ScriptMgr::addScriptFirst (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:81-107) reads a multi-line string pushed in FRONT of the running script. It trims leading blanks BEFORE testing the first character (`line.find_first_not_of(" \t")`, :90-93), so an INDENTED '#' IS a comment there - the exact opposite of the script-file rule (script.cpp:117) - and it strips a command line's own indentation (`line.substr(pos)`, :100). Its only producer today is `camera action lift_off`, which builds three engine-synthesized, comment-free lines (moveto / wait / camera action transition_to target point) and pushes them (app_command_interface.cpp:4567-4573): no author text reaches this channel, so the divergence is LATENT, not live - it becomes real the day anything pushes author text. Consequence for scedit: 'what is a comment' is a property of the CHANNEL, not of the language - file layer = column 0 only, addScriptFirst layer = first non-blank byte, live channels = never stripped. [resolves the v1 clause `comments.verify_next` and scedit/INTENT.md S5 item 3, journal 2026-08-04c; units 3/4]
comments.verify_next_RESOLVED: The v1 clause read 'script_mgr.cpp:94 has a second # site - role not yet extracted'. RESOLVED 2026-08-04: it is `inner_script_channel` above. Kept as a marker so a reader of the v1 file finds the answer.
comments.mid_line: A '#' outside a "..." run starts a comment: it and everything after it are dropped BEFORE any other transformation (the cut runs on the raw line, ahead of the leading-blank strip and the ' " ' normalisation). Quotes are counted by a plain toggle from the first byte, so a '#' inside quotes - closed or not - is ordinary text; a '#' glued to a word (abc#def) cuts at the '#'. The recorder is unaffected: it writes `commandline`, the line BEFORE the cut, so recordings keep their comments. RULED [vixy 2026-08-30]: mid-line '#' becomes a real comment, quoting-aware. ORDER RULED [vixy 2026-08-31, verbatim: "make scedit track what the HEAD would be after the behavior get corrected, then we correct spacecrafter to be in face"]: scedit models this rule first (tokenizer step 0 + the oracle's TARGET copy of parseCommand, tests/parse_oracle_test.cpp), the engine follows with the identical block at the top of parseCommand (app_command_interface.cpp:125-). Corpus at the change (408 shipped + witness + harness): '#' glued outside quotes 0, '#' inside quotes 0, word-start '#' 106 = 98 indented whole-line comments + the witness's 8 trailing ones - every one now means what its author meant. Consequences: seeds `inline-comment` and `indented-comment` retired; doc/superscript.sts:37-46 correct as written (SS-20 resolves); the future `#!` machine annotation (FEATURE_REQUESTS 2026-08-30) is a comment by this rule - its ordering clause (1) is satisfied. Written 2026-08-31, replacing the HEAD-defect description of the same date.
comments.machine_tail: `#!` is RESERVED machine syntax inside a comment [vixy 2026-08-30, FEATURE_REQUESTS "`#!` - the engine annotates the faulty script line in place"; engine 2b8ec034, ScriptAnnotator - src/scriptModule/script_annotator.hpp carries the contract]. When a script ends, the engine writes each diagnostic it raised for a file line AT THE END OF THAT LINE as ` #! <one ASCII sentence>` (several joined by `; `), after the command or the author's own `# comment`: the tail runs from the first `#!` at or after the first '#' outside quotes (ScriptAnnotator::annotationBegin uses the parser's own quote toggle, so a "#!" inside a quoted value is text) to the end of the line. Written once and REPLACED when what the engine would emit differs; a file whose tails already say this is not rewritten; a tail on a line that got no diagnostic in a run reaching the script's natural end is REMOVED (a fixed fault keeps no dead annotation); a line changed since it was loaded is skipped with a warning; an unwritable file degrades to the log. An unclosed `struct if`/`struct loop` is written at its OPENER. Producers at engine HEAD: the block-structure class only (lint_seeds carrying `engine_tail`); every failing command's debug_message is a decision pending with Vixy. For scedit: the tail is a comment to the tokenizer (mid_line) and is never composed or rewritten by the editor - only shown, with the relation to scedit's own finding for the line (agree / fixed-or-disagree / a class scedit does not check), which is the C1 signal item 15 names. EXECUTES-ONLY [added 2026-08-31 at F65; the clause the first version of this entry omitted]: only a line that EXECUTED can carry a tail. The script layer drops a line whose first byte is '#', 0, CR or LF before it is ever dispatched (script.cpp:117), so ScriptAnnotator::saw/note are never called for it - the sole call site is script_mgr.cpp:337, reached only for the lines the queue delivered to executeCommand - and ScriptAnnotator::flush iterates ONLY the notes it holds (script_annotator.cpp:130): a line it holds no note for is neither written NOR CLEARED. So a `#!` in a column-0 comment, or in an indented one (which reaches the parser and is then dropped whole by mid_line), is ordinary text the engine will never touch, exactly like a `#!` inside quotes. scedit reads it that way by construction (sc_editcore.cpp:411 - no tail unless the line HAS a command and a comment), and `--history` lists none. MEASURED on the engine's own output 2026-08-31: harness/artifacts/f63/F.sts line 1, `# F: a #! inside quotes is text`, carries no tail after a full run and scedit reports none (tests/history_cases.sts cases 7 and 8). The gap was found by an instrument: the F63 agreement harness kept its own copy of this rule, that copy lacked the clause because this entry lacked it, and it mis-read that line - which is why the rule is written down here and the copy is retired.

parse_model.unskippable_escape: Besides the three pre-table interceptions, there is a THIRD escape from the skip state: the `unskippable` flag. It is set only by AppCommandInterface::terminateScript (:291-302), tested at :361 and cleared at :365, and no script line can raise it. Reaching the end of a script runs terminateScript (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:347), so the closing `script action end` executes even inside a block left open by a `comment` with no `uncomment` - which is why an unclosed block does not leak into the next script. [units 1/3]
parse_model.pre_table_commands: comment, uncomment, struct are literal-compared BEFORE m_commands lookup (:351-358); comment/uncomment are NOT in m_commands, so the did-you-mean can never suggest them (struct is also registered). `struct`'s REGISTERED path is dead: `case SC_COMMAND::SC_STRUCT: break;` (:443) calls nothing, and the literal test at :357-358 always catches the line first. The registration (app_command_init.cpp:90) has exactly two live effects - the did-you-mean candidate list and the recorder's enum-to-name map (app_command_init.cpp:111-127). [unit 4]
parse_model.executeCommand_reentry: A handler may call executeCommand AGAIN, and executeCommand clears `command`/`args` and replaces `commandline` on entry (:332-335). Two sites: `media`'s audio-only path rebuilds an `audio ...` line by string concatenation and re-enters (:3676), and `clear` runs ~35 nested commands (:2642-2693). What a line-level reader must know: (a) the nested call destroys the outer handler's own `args`, `debug_message` and `commandline`; (b) the recorder records `commandline` at status time (:1311), so what is RECORDED is the nested or rebuilt line - `clear` never records itself and leaves the LAST nested line behind, and `media`'s rebuilt line has lost the quoting that grouped a filename with spaces, so such a name is destroyed; (c) the rebuilt `audio` line ends in a dangling `loop` key when `loop` was absent, harmless only because pair extraction drops it silently. The whole recorder-rewrite class - these two plus `flag` (:1355) and `timerate action increment|decrement|sincrement|sdecrement` (:3506, :3523, :3539, :3555) rewriting their own line, plus `set` recording once PER PAIR (:2394) - is [registered upstream] as claude/INTENT.md S5.96. Consequence for scedit: a round-trip through a recording is never an identity. [units 2/3]
parse_model.value_domains_are_per_branch: A key's value domain belongs to the (command, BRANCH) pair, not to the command. The same key in the same handler is read two different ways: `zoom duration` is Utility::strToPosDouble on the `auto` branch (raw text, no $-substitution, sign discarded) and evalDouble on the `fov`/`center` branches (:3435 vs :3453, :3459); `media subtitle` (:3776 vs :3927) and `media speed` (:3849 vs :3917) likewise carry two readings each. A tool that maps key -> domain per COMMAND is unfaithful. This file therefore carries `branches` on the selector-shaped commands, and each key's `notes` names the branch its domain belongs to. [unit 3]

boolean_grammars._statement: At least FOUR readings of a boolean-looking value coexist in the command surface. A lint that assumes the flag grammar for every boolean-looking value is WRONG: the grammar is a per-KEY fact, and each key's own `value` field states it.
boolean_grammars.isTrue_family: Utility::isTrue (src/tools/utility.hpp:160-171): the single character '1', or 'on'/'true' case-insensitively - nothing else. Used for flag values and for the keys display/fader/nopause/loop/mipmap/persistent/keycolor (unit 2), `zoom manual`, `media loop`/`keycolor`/`subtitle` (unit 3). Its mirror Utility::isFalse (:172-181) reads `select pointer`.
boolean_grammars.strToBool_with_default: Utility::strToBool(value, default): an unrecognized value takes the DEFAULT, not false - `configuration binary_mode` (unit 2).
boolean_grammars.literal_on: an exact comparison against the word 'on': `image` accelerate_alt/accelerate_az/decelerate_alt/decelerate_az (:3204-3225, unit 2) and `zoom center` (unit 3). 'true' and '1' mean NO there.
boolean_grammars.literal_true_W_TRUE: an exact comparison against the word 'true' (W_TRUE): `camera action follow_rotation value <v>` (:4608, unit 4). 'on', '1' and 'TRUE' all mean NO there - this is the only W_TRUE use in the tree.
boolean_grammars.consequence: the `silent-off-value` lint is armed ONLY where commandFlag's own value grammar applies (flag_value_grammar below). Everywhere else the domain is the key's.

flag_value_grammar.accepted: toggle | on-values via Utility::isTrue | EVERYTHING ELSE silently means OFF
flag_value_grammar.consequence: a typo in a flag value is a silent 'off' -- no diagnostic exists engine-side

parse_model.flag_multi_pair: SCOPE, corrected at the args merge. The single-pair restriction covers EXACTLY ten commands: `flag` (:1346 reads args.begin() and never loops - the code says so itself, '// could loop if want to allow that syntax' :1345) and the nine variable commands define (:4649), add (:4663), sub (:4676), multiply (:4690), divide (:4703), modulo (:4716), tangent (:4729), trunc (:4742), sinus (:4755). On such a line only the ALPHABETICALLY first key is applied, silently: `add b 2 a 1` changes `a`. It does NOT extend to `set` - see set_multi_pair. [units 1/4]
parse_model.set_multi_pair: `set` is MULTI-pair: commandSet loops over EVERY pair (:2282-2285) and applies each through evalCommandSet, folding the results with `&&` (:2284). Two consequences the author cannot see: the pairs act in ALPHABETICAL key order, so `set star_scale 2 home_planet Mars` changes the home planet first; and because executeCommandStatus() returns false once debug_message is set (:1315-1330) while debug_message is cleared only once per LINE (:330), the FIRST failing pair makes every later pair fail too - one unknown name and the rest of the line never applies. [unit 2]
parse_model.unknown_command: debug_message 'Unrecognized or malformed command name' + Levenshtein nearest-neighbour suggestion over the family list (searchNeighbour, app_command_init.cpp:388-407; no distance threshold -- a suggestion is always produced, log-only). scedit reproduces searchNeighbour exactly (no threshold) in its tokenizer library; what it CAPS is only the DISPLAY of the suggestion in a diagnostic - see lint_seeds `unknown-command` and util/scedit/tests/derivation-diff.md S5.7
parse_model.recording_alias_loss: CORRECTED 2026-08-31 (the earlier text claimed a recorded `flyto` round-trips as `camera`): a recording writes the line AS TYPED -- ScriptMgr::recordCommand (script_mgr.cpp:254) receives `commandline`, the raw input -- and m_commands_ToString (the enum-to-name map) has NO consumer at this revision, so no alias is respelled anywhere. The one re-serialisation is `flag <name> toggle`, rewritten as `flag <name> <0|1>` from m_flags_ToString (app_command_interface.cpp:476-478). The map itself is now built CANONICAL-FIRST (app_command_init.cpp:99-111, aliases added after :112-118), so a future consumer names `camera`/`divide`/`multiply`/`modulo`, never `flyto`/`div`/`mul`/`mod`; until 2026-08-31 it came from the alphabetical name map and `camera` won only by sort order. Lint seed 'alias-respelled' retired with this correction: an alias has no user-facing consequence to report.
parse_model.if_structure: `struct if` is a STACK, not a flag: IfSwap holds a std::vector<bool> (src/interfaceModule/if_swap.hpp:85). `struct if <cond>` pushes (commandStruct :4781-4828; the pushed value is TRUE when the test FAILS - push(true) means skip), `struct if else` flips the top (:4771-4775 -> revert, if_swap.cpp:73-81), `struct if end` pops (:4776-4780 -> pop, :40-54). The skip test at :361 reads get(), which is the OR over the stack (defineCommandSwap :90): one true entry anywhere skips everything. A closer on an empty stack is LOGGED as an error and ignored ('end without if' :45 @ 2fe14699 [NOT AT HEAD: the referent left this file: IfSwap::pop now returns false and the caller reports], 'else without if' :76 @ 2fe14699 [NOT AT HEAD: the referent left this file: IfSwap::revert now returns false and the caller reports]). The whole if-case is guarded by `swapCommand != true` (:4770): inside a `comment` block no `struct if` line counts, `end` included. `struct` lines are intercepted BEFORE the skip test (:357-358 vs :361), so an `end` inside a skipped region still pops - which is what makes nesting work. The stack is cleared only by `script action end` (:2973), which the end of every script runs (terminateScript :291-302 <- script_mgr.cpp:347): an opener left open discards its own file's tail and nothing after. Static consequence: an opener with no `end` before EOF is a defect on every runtime path; lint `unclosed-struct` (reported at the OPENER), `end-without-if`, `else-without-if`. Witness: doc/superscript.sts:1404-1409 (six openers, the comparison catalogue - `a inf b` pushes skip iff a >= b and `a sup b` iff a <= b, one of them holds for any a, b, so the tail from :1405 is skipped deterministically) and :1547 (SS-24); shipped fscripts/panorama5.sts:102 @ 2fe14699 [NOT AT HEAD: field data, not a file of this repository] (SS-25). RULED 2026-08-30 [vixy]: the engine will LOG the unclosed if (three-part schema) and annotate the opener with a `#!` tail; the if-state will be scoped to the script in the non-legacy exec policies. Added 2026-08-31.
parse_model.loop_structure: `struct loop <n>` .. `struct loop end` is NOT a stack engine-side: one isInLoop / loopVector / nbrLoop (script_mgr.hpp:127-138, script_mgr.cpp:268-274). `struct loop <n>` with n > 1 (:4863-4875; n through evalString then strToInt) starts copying the following lines; `struct loop end` (:4844-4853) stops copying and replays them nbrLoop-1 times (initIterator :127-133 pops the `end` line itself, the replay loop is script_mgr.cpp:310-328); `struct loop break` (:4855-4861) abandons the repetition and leaves the pair syntactically open; n < 1 raises the skip flag (:4868-4869) that only `struct loop end` lowers. The loop case is guarded by `ifSwap->get() != true` (:4843) - a runtime fact. Static consequence: an opener with no `end` before EOF is a defect on every path - n > 1: the block runs once and never repeats; n < 1: the tail is skipped; lint `unclosed-struct`. `struct loop end` with no loop open resets an empty loop and logs NOTHING; lint `loop-end-without-loop`. Not in the corpus (`struct loop 2`, `3600`, `4` only, all closed). Added 2026-08-31.

commands._source: app_command_init.cpp:37-126 (registration; aliases block :112-118) x base_command_interface.hpp:328-398 (spellings); enum SC_COMMAND base_command_interface.hpp:32-38
commands._args_status: args specs EXTRACTED for every command (2026-08-04, the per-handler sweep of app_command_interface.cpp, 4 units, count-gated 339/339 `args[` lines). Per-key facts: `doc`, `value` (domain), `values` (when enumerated), `value_docs` (per value, when each selects a different effect), `default` (or the ABSENT-key behaviour stated explicitly), `required` (tri-state: true / false / "conditional"), `source` (file:line), `notes`, and `downstream` (true = the key is not read in the handler at all: the handler forwards the whole args map and the key is read in another file, anchored there). Command-level: `branches` for selector-shaped handlers, `exclusive_groups`, `key_grammar` for the commands whose key is not from a fixed list, `notes`, `flagged` (C2 gaps for Vixy - never invented).
commands._doc_status: doc = one plain-language line at the zero-knowledge bar (see _meta.documentation_requirement), on every command AND every key. Filled from the handler code only; `null` + an entry in `flagged` is the honest state where the code cannot answer.
commands._schema_note: Per-entry fields and who reads them. `enum`/`handler`/`subfamily`/`alias_of` are the v1 identity. `unit` names the sweep fragment this entry's content came from (grammar/args/unit-<N>.json) -- that fragment is where a correction goes first. `lines` is the handler's extent in app_command_interface.cpp. `registration` is a SOURCE ANCHOR (app_command_init.cpp line + the ACP_CN_* macro and its spelling) - it is NOT the pre-table marker any more. `pretable: true` marks the two commands compared as literals BEFORE the m_commands lookup (comment, uncomment): they are accepted by the engine but are absent from `commandList`, so a did-you-mean can never suggest them. `args_complete` (on every entry) answers ONE question: 'is the key vocabulary in `args` the whole vocabulary this command accepts?' false = there are more legal keys than are listed here, so no consumer may report an unlisted key as unknown; the reason and the owning work item are in the entry's `flagged`/`notes`. For a command with an empty `args` and a `key_grammar` (flag, print, set, comment, uncomment, define/add/sub/multiply/divide/modulo/tangent/trunc/sinus, flyto), `args_complete` says nothing extra: `key_grammar` already states that the key is not drawn from a fixed list of this command's own.

add.doc: Add a number to a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is the number to add to it.
key_grammar.key_domain: a name given earlier by `define`, or one of the four reserved names that can be written (longitude, latitude, altitude, heading -- families.reserved_variables); a name that was never defined is CREATED and set to the value written, with the log line "Not possible to operate with undefined variable so define to null from ops"
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable (its value is used)
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command_addition"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4663-4665) -- the handler even says so: '// could loop if want to allow that syntax' (:4662).

Writing to a reserved name works for the four that have a setter (longitude, latitude, altitude, heading); the others log "No setter with reserved variable <name>. Do nothing." (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:348-376).

Reserved names take a SECOND path in the same call: after the reserved value is written the code falls on to the ordinary-variable branch, which does not find the name and tries to define it -- which is refused, printing "<name> is a reservedVar so you can't define it" (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:205-214 then :137-141). The arithmetic still happened.

mode.doc: Jump between the four scales the program can show: the solar system, the stars around it, the galaxy, and the universe.

jump.value: enumerated, matched without regard to case

value_docs.in_solarsystem: the scale of the solar system, seen from a body or from space near one (spelling 'insolarsystem' does the same)
value_docs.in_stellarsystem: the scale of another star's system (spelling 'instellarsystem' does the same)
value_docs.in_galaxy: the scale of the galaxy around the solar system (spelling 'ingalaxy' does the same)
value_docs.in_universe: the scale of the universe beyond the galaxy (spelling 'inuniverse' does the same)

jump.default: absent or empty -> the command does NOTHING AT ALL and still reports success: `body` and `altitude` are inside the same test (:3633-3651)
jump.notes: The value is put into lower case before it is compared (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:86), so IN_GALAXY works too. A value that is none of the eight does not report an error and does not stay put either: the present scale is left and re-entered and whatever was selected is dropped (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:88, 101-103).

body.doc: Which body to stand on after the jump; the word selected means the object selected right now.
body.value: string (a body's English name), or the word selected
body.default: absent or empty -> you stay on the body you are on
body.notes: Read only when `jump` is present. A name no body answers to leaves you where you are (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2165).

altitude.doc: How high to stand after the jump, in metres; a value starting with + or - is added to your present height instead.
altitude.default: absent or empty -> your height is unchanged
altitude.notes: Read only when `jump` is present. The move is immediate (the duration passed is 0, :3649). The + / - test looks at the first character of the text (:3645), exactly as `moveto alt` does.

branches.effect: change scale, then optionally the body you stand on, then optionally your height
nothing happens; no message is set, so the command reports SUCCESS and is recorded

notes: `mode body Mars` or `mode altitude 1000` on their own do nothing whatever: both keys live inside the `jump` test.

The name `mode` is also one of the 43 setting names (`set mode <value>`), which is recorded as parsing, reporting success and calling nothing (families.set_names.known_defective). The two are unrelated surfaces with the same spelling.
Changing scale always drops the selection, even when the scale does not actually change (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:101-102).

body_trace.doc: Draw the trail a body leaves on the sky as time runs, as if it held a pen.

pen.doc: Put the pen down (start drawing the trail), lift it (stop), or change it to whichever it is not.
values: off-forms per Utility::isFalse ("0", "off", "false", case-insensitive; src/tools/utility.hpp:172-183) = pen up
pen.default: absent -> the command goes on to `action`, `target`, `hide`; present with any other value -> "Command 'body_trace': unknown pen value"
pen.notes: This is the one boolean in the unit that has a real THIRD state: unlike `flag`, a value that is neither true-form nor false-form nor toggle is reported as an error instead of silently meaning off.

target.value: string -- a body name, or the word 'selected' for whatever is selected right now
target.default: absent -> the body last chosen stays the one being traced
target.notes: A name no body answers to logs 'Unknown planet_name in bodyTraceBodyChange' and changes nothing (src/bodyModule/protosystem.cpp:468-475) -- the command still reports success.

action.doc: Erase the trail drawn so far.
action.default: absent or any other value -> this branch is not taken

hide.doc: Show or stop showing one of the trails already drawn -- give its number, or 'all' for every one.
hide.default: absent -> this branch is not taken
hide.notes: It TOGGLES rather than hides: each call flips the chosen trail's visibility ('bodyData[n].hide = !bodyData[n].hide', body_trace.cpp:68,71). There are 7 trails, numbered 0-6 (NB_MAX_LIST, src/bodyModule/body_trace.hpp:40); a number >= 7 does nothing (body_trace.cpp:64). A non-numeric word becomes 0 (Utility::strToInt, src/tools/utility.cpp:448).

branches.effect: optionally change the traced body, then put the pen down/up/toggle
erase the drawn trails
change which body is traced
flip one trail's visibility
"command 'body_trace' : unknown argument"

notes: Only ONE branch runs per line: each returns immediately (:1758, :1762, :1778, :1782, :1786). With `pen` present the branch order means `action clear` and `hide` on the same line are ignored.
`target` and `hide` are tested with `!= ""` rather than `.empty()` (:1752, :1780, :1784) -- same meaning, noted only because it is the shape a mechanical extractor sees.

body.doc: Act on the objects of a star system: add one, remove one, hide it, recolour it, or change how it is drawn.

action.doc: What to do; every other key on the line depends on this word.

value_docs.load: Add an object. With `mode` it adds a three-dimensional model file (see `mode`); without it, it adds a body to the star system, described by the same keys a system data file uses.
value_docs.remove: Remove one three-dimensional model, by `name`, from the scene named by `mode` (this value is only read on the model path).
value_docs.clear: With `mode`: remove every model from that scene. Without `mode`: remove every body a script has added, keeping the ones the data file declared.
value_docs.drop: Remove the one body called `name` (only bodies a script added can be removed).
value_docs.initial: Put every body back to the state its data file declared, and show or hide it as that file said.
value_docs.reload: Read the current system's data file again, keeping where you stand and what time it is: edits to the file take effect, bodies removed from it disappear, bodies added to it appear.
value_docs.save: Write the current system to a system file, so that the bodies a script pushed in this session are ordinary data at the next start.
value_docs.preload: Fetch a body's big picture files into memory now, so that arriving there later does not stall (see `keep_time` and `purge`).
value_docs.dual_dump: Development tool: write a machine-readable record of both drawing paths' state to a file.
value_docs.screenshot: Take a picture of the screen through the program's own capture path (development tool).

action.default: absent -> the command tries the `skin_use`/`skin_tex` forms, then the `name` form, then `tesselation`; present with any other word -> "command 'body' : unknown action argument"
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4113, 4119-4135 (model path), 3989-4044 (system path) (W_ACTION="action", W_LOAD="load", W_REMOVE="remove", ACP_CN_CLEAR="clear", W_DROP="drop", W_INITIAL="initial", W_RELOAD="reload", W_SAVE="save", W_PRELOAD="preload": base_command_interface.hpp:81,103,296,335,156,200,313,148,312)
action.notes: "dual_dump" (:4196) and "screenshot" (:4199) are bare string literals with no W_* token -- harness routes, kept in the surface because they are reachable from any script.

name.doc: Which body the line is about, written as its English name.

value_docs.home_planet: the body you are standing on: the handler replaces this word by that body's name before doing anything else (:4115)
value_docs.all: on the `color` form only, every body at once (src/bodyModule/solarsystem_color.cpp:37-39)
value_docs.selected: on the `skin_use`/`skin_tex` forms, the body currently selected (src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:1423-1431); on `action preload`, likewise (src/coreModule/core.cpp:984-990)

Only `datum_radius`/`ground_radius` report an unknown body to the script.

mode.doc: Say which of the three scenes a three-dimensional model file belongs to; writing it switches the whole line to the model form.

value_docs.in_universe: the scene drawn when you are outside the galaxy
value_docs.in_galaxy: the scene drawn when you are inside the galaxy

The three words are bare literals in the handler (:4119); OjmMgr::convert maps anything else to OTHER, but the handler never gets there because its own test already failed.

filename.doc: The file to read or write, depending on the action.
filename.default: on the model form: absent -> the built name is "/.ojm" and no model is found; on `action save`: absent -> this system's own file; on `action dual_dump`: absent -> /tmp/dual_trace.json; on `action screenshot`: absent -> an automatic name <base>-YY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS.png

values: on-forms per Utility::isTrue (src/tools/utility.hpp:160-171: "1", "on", "true", case-insensitive) = use the alternative picture
ANYTHING ELSE = use the ordinary picture, silently

hidden.default: absent -> this form is not taken; present with any other value -> "Command 'body': unknown hidden value"

orbit.doc: Draw the line of this body's orbit (yes) or stop drawing it (no).
values: off-forms per Utility::isFalse = do not draw
orbit.default: absent -> this form is not taken; present with any other value -> "Command 'body': unknown orbit value"

color.doc: Which of this body's colours to change.

value_docs.halo: the glow drawn around the body
value_docs.label: the body's name written on the sky
value_docs.trail: the trail it leaves behind it

completable_excluded.xRRGGBB: a SHAPE, not a value: RR/GG/BB stand for two hexadecimal digits each

ground_radius.default: absent -> this form is not taken

tesselation.doc: Which of the surface-detail settings to change; the number goes in `value`.

value_docs.min_tes_level: the least amount of surface detail used
value_docs.max_tes_level: the most amount of surface detail used
value_docs.planet_altimetry_level: how strongly the relief of planets is raised
value_docs.moon_altimetry_level: how strongly the relief of moons is raised
value_docs.earth_altimetry_level: how strongly the relief of the Earth is raised

tesselation.notes: This form is only reached when NO `name` was given (:4212, :4305): `body name Mars tesselation ...` takes the name form and reports "case name unknown argument".

value.doc: The number for the chosen surface-detail setting.

The four keys the immediate downstream names first are listed with `downstream: true`; the rest are not listed, so NO consumer may call an unlisted key of `body` unknown.

A `mode` value outside the three words with a valid system `action` silently takes the SYSTEM path (the test at :4119 fails and `mode` is then never looked at again) -- e.g. `body mode in_galaxie action clear` removes every script-added BODY instead of the models of a scene.

camera.signature: commandCamera(uint64_t &wait) -- writes the script's inter-command delay on the two `move_to` forms (executeCommand :389)
camera.doc: Move the point of view about the universe: name a place, go to it, turn towards a body, or fly up from where you stand.

action.doc: What to do with the point of view; every other key on the line depends on this word.

value_docs.rotate: turn the view towards the place you are standing on, over `duration` seconds
value_docs.align_with: tilt the view so that the named place's own up direction becomes yours, over `duration` seconds
value_docs.transition_to: change what the view is attached to, without travelling: either the place you stand right now, or a body
value_docs.move_to: travel to a point of space or to a body, over `duration`
value_docs.save: write where the view is, and when, into a file
value_docs.load: put the view back where such a file says
value_docs.free_mode: switch free flight on or off
value_docs.descend: go down towards, or up away from, what you are looking at
value_docs.lift_off: climb to a given height and then detach the view from the body
value_docs.create: declare a new named place the view can be attached to
value_docs.switch: attach the view to a named place
value_docs.follow_rotation: say whether the view turns with the body it is attached to

action.default: absent -> "command 'camera' : action argument"; present with any other word -> "command 'camera' : missing name" when no `name` was given, else "command 'camera' : unknown action argument"
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4354, 4357-4360, 4362, 4373, 4397, 4432, 4496, 4511, 4526, 4539, 4553, 4576-4616 (W_ROTATE="rotate", W_ALIGN_WITH="align_with", W_TRANSITION_TO="transition_to", W_MOVE_TO="move_to", W_SAVE="save", W_LOAD="load", W_FREE_MODE="free_mode", W_DESCEND="descend", W_LIFT_OFF="lift_off", W_CREATE="create", W_DROP="drop", W_SWITCH="switch", W_FOLLOW_ROTATION="follow_rotation": base_command_interface.hpp:155,252,251,250,148,103,246,247,249,226,156,229,245)

name.doc: The name of a place the view can be attached to (its own name, not a body's).
name.default: absent -> the four forms that need it are refused with "command 'camera' : missing name", which is ALSO what an unknown action reports
name.notes: On `action transition_to target body` the same key means a BODY name instead (:4414) -- the only place in this handler where it does.

value_docs.point: on `transition_to`: the exact place you are standing right now becomes a named place called temp_point; on `move_to`: the point given by `x`, `y` and `z`
value_docs.body: a body: named by `name` on `transition_to`, by `body_name` on `move_to`

target.default: absent -> "command 'camera' : missing target" (rotate: "missing target"; transition_to and move_to: their own message); present with any other word -> "command 'transition_to' : unknown target arg" / "command 'camera' : unknown target arg"
target.notes: ON `action rotate` THE VALUE IS NOT USED: it must be non-empty, but the movement always goes to the place you are standing on -- Core::lookAnchor ignores its name argument (the per-name branch is commented out, src/coreModule/core.cpp:2632-2642).

duration.doc: How long the movement takes, in seconds.
duration.default: on `rotate`: absent -> 2 seconds; on `align_with`: absent -> 0 (immediate); on `move_to target point`: absent -> the jump is immediate; on `move_to target body`: absent -> "command 'move_to body' : missing a body_name or time"; on `lift_off`: absent -> 3 seconds
duration.notes: On both `move_to` forms the script ALSO waits: the delay before the next command is set to this many seconds (:4458, :4487 -- evalInt(value) x 1000 milliseconds, so a fractional duration is cut down to whole seconds for the wait but not for the movement). The travel itself is measured in simulated time: the seconds are divided by 86400 and the arrival is that many days later on the simulation clock (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:430, 464).

body.doc: On `action align_with`, the name of the place (declared with `action create`, of the kind that follows a body) whose up direction the view should take.
body.notes: Despite the key name it is looked up among the declared PLACES, not among the bodies, and the place must be one that follows a body; otherwise the log says "anchor not found" / "wrong anchor type" and the command reports "error align_with_body body".

body_name.doc: On `action move_to target body`, which body to travel to.
body_name.default: absent -> "command 'move_to body' : missing a body_name or time"
body_name.notes: As with `body` above, the name is looked up among the declared PLACES that follow a body (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:491-497), so only bodies that have such a place declared can be travelled to.

x.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the first coordinate, counted from the Sun.
x.notes: The three numbers are a position in the heliocentric ecliptic frame (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:387-395, 405-442). The unit is NOT stated on this path: astronomical units is [derived] from two facts about the same frame -- the km->AU divisor applied to `altitude` beside it (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:475, with AU declared in kilometres at src/tools/sc_const.hpp:45), and the new-path anchor code, which says 'a fixed point x/y/z in AU' of the same coordinates (src/experimentalModule/CameraAnchors.cpp:141). On `action create` the same three spellings are read again downstream, for a fixed place (see the downstream keys).

y.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the second coordinate, counted from the Sun.

z.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the third coordinate, counted from the Sun.

altitude.doc: On `move_to`, how high above the body to stop, in kilometres; on `lift_off`, the height to climb to, in whatever unit the `moveto` command reads (see notes).
altitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible; kilometres on `move_to target body` [derived: the value is divided by AU, and AU is declared in kilometres]
altitude.default: on `move_to target body`: absent -> stop at five times the body's own radius; on `lift_off`: absent -> "command 'camera lift_off' : missing altitude"
altitude.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4475, 4479-4482 (move_to body), 4390, 4393-4396, 4404 (lift_off) -> src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:475 ('alt/AU', with AU in kilometres, src/tools/sc_const.hpp:45) (W_ALTITUDE="altitude", base_command_interface.hpp:179)
altitude.notes: On `lift_off` the value is not used directly: it is written into a `moveto altitude <value> duration <duration>` line (:4569), i.e. it becomes the `moveto` command's own altitude argument (unit 3).

filename.doc: The file to write the view into, or to read it back from.
filename.default: on `action save`: absent -> the name 'anchor' (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:371); on `action load`: absent -> "command 'camera load' : missing file name"
filename.notes: The file written holds the place's declaration plus your height, longitude, latitude, the date and the direction you look in (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:722-733). DEFECT, recorded not fixed: the folder 'anchors/' is prepended TWICE on both paths (src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:65 and src/bodyModule/ssystem_factory.hpp:1006; likewise :70 and :1010), so the file actually used is anchors/anchors/<name>, relative to the folder the program was started in.

state.doc: On `action free_mode`, whether free flight is on.
values: on-forms per Utility::isTrue = free flight on
state.notes: Same silent-off class as `flag`: a typo means 'off' with no diagnostic. New drawing path only.

coef.doc: On `action descend`, how much closer to go: less than 1 goes down, more than 1 goes up (0.5 halves the distance, 2 doubles it).
coef.notes: What it goes down towards depends on where you are: the ground under the view ray when a body is close, the last selected body when you are out among the systems (src/experimentalModule/Camera.cpp:1059-1082). New drawing path only.

value.doc: On `action follow_rotation`, whether the view turns with the body: write exactly the word true for yes.
value.notes: SHARP EDGE: this is the only boolean of the unit that is NOT read with the usual on/1/true grammar -- the test is an exact string comparison against `true`, so `on`, `1` and `TRUE` all mean NO here.

type.doc: On `action create`, what kind of place is being declared.

value_docs.point: a fixed place, given by x, y and z
value_docs.observatory: a fixed place, given by x, y and z (the same thing as point for the newer drawing path)
value_docs.body: a place attached to the body named by body_name
value_docs.orbit: a place that follows an orbit, around parent or around the fixed point orbit_center_x/y/z

type.default: absent -> the place is not created; both registries log what was expected

follow_rotation.doc: On `action create` with type body, whether the place turns with the body.
follow_rotation.default: absent -> the place does not declare it

parent.doc: On `action create` with type orbit, the body the orbit goes around.
parent.default: absent -> the orbit must instead be given a centre with orbit_center_x/y/z

orbit_center_x.doc: On `action create` with type orbit and no parent, the centre of the orbit: first coordinate, in astronomical units.
orbit_center_x.default: absent -> the place is not created

orbit_center_y.doc: On `action create` with type orbit and no parent, the centre of the orbit: second coordinate, in astronomical units.
orbit_center_y.default: absent -> the place is not created

orbit_center_z.doc: On `action create` with type orbit and no parent, the centre of the orbit: third coordinate, in astronomical units.
orbit_center_z.default: absent -> the place is not created

coord_func.doc: On `action create` with type orbit, which kind of orbit describes the movement.
coord_func.value: string -- the orbit-kind names of the stellar-system-file grammar
coord_func.default: absent -> no orbit can be built and the place is not created
coord_func.notes: The orbit's own numbers are the same keys a body's orbit uses (INTENT S5 item 4) -- see `flagged`.

branches.effect: turn the view towards the place you stand on (the target VALUE is not used); duration defaults to 2 s
tilt the view to that place's up direction; failure gives "error align_with_body body"
detach the view where it stands, as a place called temp_point; failure gives "error transition_to point"
attach the view to that body without travelling; failure gives "error transition_to body"
travel to that point; with a duration the script also waits that long; failure gives "error move_to point"
travel to that body and stop at `altitude` km above it (default: five radii); the script waits `duration`; failure gives "error move_to body"
write the view's place, height, date and direction to a file; failure gives "error saving camera"
read such a file back; failure gives "error loading CameraAnchor"
switch free flight on or off
go down towards, or up away from, what you look at
queue three commands in front of the script: climb to that height, wait, then detach the view; duration defaults to 3
declare a new named place in both registries; failure gives "error creating CameraAnchor"
forget that place (refused while the view is attached to it); failure gives "error drop CameraAnchor"
attach the view to that place; failure gives "error switch CameraAnchor"
say whether the view turns with the body; failure gives "error camera follow_rotation"
"command 'camera' : missing name" when no `name` was given (the name test comes FIRST, :4576), otherwise "command 'camera' : unknown action argument"

camera.args_complete_reason: downstream vocabulary DEFERRED, not missing: `camera action create` forwards the whole parsed map (:4583) to TWO anchor registries that read different vocabularies for the same declaration (src/navModule/anchor_creator_cor.cpp, src/experimentalModule/CameraAnchors.cpp). The keys the registries share are listed with `downstream: true`; the rest are not, so NO consumer may call an unlisted key of `camera` unknown.
notes: The `name` test at :4576 sits between the two groups of actions: every action listed before it works without a name, every one after it needs one -- and any UNKNOWN action word is reported as a missing name when none was written, which is a misleading message for a misspelt action.

C1-relevant: `action lift_off` does not act itself -- it builds a three-line script (moveto / wait / camera action transition_to target point) and pushes it in front of the running script (:4567-4573). Those three lines are parsed by ScriptMgr::addScriptFirst (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:81-107), whose comment rule differs from the file loader's: there an INDENTED '#' IS dropped as a comment (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:90-97), while at the script-file layer only a '#' in the first column is (src/scriptModule/script.cpp:117, parse_model.comments).

C1-relevant: `action lift_off` returns addScriptFirst's value directly (:4573) instead of executeCommandStatus(), so the line is never recorded by the recorder and never reports a failure -- addScriptFirst always returns true (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:106).

`action create` forwards the whole parsed map (:4583) to TWO registries which read DIFFERENT vocabularies for the same declaration: the old one accepts type point/observatory/body/orbit with x/y/z, body_name, parent, orbit_center_* (src/navModule/anchor_creator_cor.cpp), the new one the same plus follow_rotation and the orbit keys, and refuses with an explaining log line (src/experimentalModule/CameraAnchors.cpp:116-145). The command reports success when EITHER registry accepted (src/bodyModule/ssystem_factory.hpp:884-889).

`action rotate`, `align_with`, `move_to target body` and `align_with` all look their name up among the DECLARED PLACES, not among the bodies: without a place declared for a body (by `action create`, or by the anchor file the program reads at start), those forms cannot reach it.
flagged: camera `action create` orbit keys: the orbit's own numbers (coord_func + the orbit_* family) are the stellar-system-file orbit grammar, INTENT S5 item 4 -- not enumerated here for the same reason as `body action load` (I2). Recorded: the anchor-level keys and both registries' entry points. SCOPE DECISION, for the supervisor.

camera anchors/anchors double prefix (`action save` / `action load`, src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:65,70 x src/bodyModule/ssystem_factory.hpp:1006,1010): a real path defect found while extracting. Recorded, not fixed (out of scope). Until it is decided, the doc line cannot honestly promise where the file lands, so it states what the code does. Vixy/supervisor: is this a fix or a documented path?

Whether the editor should offer completion for a key whose value does nothing -- and whether the intent was to restore the branch -- is not answerable from the code. Vixy.

clear.doc: Put the sky back to a known plain state: standing on Earth, real time rate, starting view, all labels and lines off, stars, planets and nebulae on.

state.doc: Which plain state to go to.

value_docs.variable: forget the script's own variables and change NOTHING else
value_docs.natural: the ordinary view from the ground: air and ground scenery ON
value_docs.<anything else>: the same reset with air and ground scenery OFF (the view from space)

state.default: absent -> the last branch: the same reset with the air and the ground scenery switched OFF

notes: Everything but `state variable` is a fixed list of other commands run one after another (:2642-2693): set home_planet Earth, the atmosphere/landscape pair, the saved grid/display/line states, about thirty `flag ... off`, three `flag ... on`, then `deselect`, `timerate rate 1` and `zoom auto initial` (the last three spelled DESELECT / TIMERATE_RATE_1 / ZOOM_AUTO_INITIAL, base_command_interface.hpp:653-655).

C1-relevant: those nested calls go through the full executeCommand (:305-309 -> :312), which CLEARS `args` and `debug_message` and REPLACES `commandline` (:330-338). commandClear reads its own `state` first (:2633), so it is unaffected, but any tool modelling 'the args of this line' must know the map is destroyed mid-handler.

Recorder consequence, recorded not fixed: when recording, `clear` writes the ~35 nested lines into the recorded script and never writes `clear` itself; because `commandline` is left holding the LAST nested line, the final executeCommandStatus() (:2695) records "zoom auto initial" a second time.
`clear state variable` returns immediately (:2635-2638): none of the sky changes happen.

color.doc: Set the colour of a named sky annotation (lines, grids, labels, ...).

property.default: absent or empty -> "Command 'color': unknown expected argument 'property'"; unknown name -> "Command 'color': unknown property" plus a nearest-name suggestion in the log

completable_excluded.xRRGGBB: a SHAPE, not a value: RR/GG/BB stand for two hexadecimal digits each

r.default: absent -> 0 when either of g or b is given; all three absent AND `value` absent -> "'color': missing expected argument 'r' or 'g' or 'b'"

index.doc: Which entry of the star colour table to set -- only 'property star_table' uses it.
index.default_value_source: app_command_interface.cpp:2050 (unguarded args[] lookup) -> app_command_eval.cpp:116-133 -> src/tools/utility.cpp:399-406 (strToDouble catches and returns default_value 0, utility.hpp:143)

(The same by-value slip does not affect the hex and rgb-word paths, whose messages are set on the reference: :103, :113, :119, :145, :149.)

configuration.doc: Load or save the program's settings, or load and save the star-line and star-catalogue files.

action.doc: What to do.

value_docs.load: without `module`: re-read the settings file and restart the program's setup. With `module`: read the named file into that module.
value_docs.save: without `module`: write the current settings back to the settings file. With `module`: write that module's data to the named file.
value_docs.clear: only with `module`: empty that module (drop the loaded lines or stars).
value_docs.load_star: only with `module star_lines`: add the lines of one bright star by catalogue number.

action.default: absent -> "command 'configuration': unknown argument"
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:2409, 2415, 2427, 2436, 2440, 2453, 2465, 2493, 2502-2510 (W_ACTION="action" base_command_interface.hpp:81; W_LOAD="load" :103, W_SAVE="save" :148, W_CLEAR="clear" :90, W_LOAD_STAR="load_star" :104)

module.doc: Which part of the program to act on; leave it out to act on the settings file itself.

value_docs.star_lines: the drawn lines that join stars
value_docs.star_navigator: the star catalogue used when travelling among the stars

module.default: absent -> the command acts on the settings file (action load = re-read them, action save = write them)
module.notes: An unrecognised module name sets "command 'configuration': unknown module argument" but does NOT stop the command - see the command notes.

name.doc: The file to read or write.
name.value: string(evalString on the load paths) - $-variable substitution possible
name.default: absent with `module star_lines` -> "command 'configuration' missing name parameter"; absent with `module star_navigator` -> "command 'configuration', star_navigator missing name argument"
name.notes: On `action load` the name is evaluated and looked for in the script folder first, then used as written (FilePath TFP::DATA, src/tools/file_path.cpp:102-145); a file that does not exist gives "command 'configuration' filename not found". On `action save` the name is used exactly as written, unevaluated.

binary_mode.doc: Whether the file is in the compact binary form rather than plain text.
binary_mode.default: absent or empty -> false (plain text); "true" or "1" (any capitalisation) -> true; anything else -> false
binary_mode.notes: Not used by `action clear` or `action load_star`; ignored on `star_navigator action load` unless `mode sc`.

mode.doc: Which layout the star catalogue file is written in.

value_docs.sc: spacecrafter's own layout - the only one that also honours `binary_mode`

mode.default: absent or empty with `module star_navigator action load` -> "command 'configuration', star_navigator missing mode argument"; an unknown value -> "command 'configuration': unknown starNavigator mode parameter"
mode.source: app_command_interface.cpp:2466, 2472-2490 (key spelled ACP_SC_MODE="mode", base_command_interface.hpp:589; W_RAW="raw" :257, W_SC="sc" :258, W_OTHER="other" :259)
mode.notes: C2/vocabulary note: this KEY is spelled with ACP_SC_MODE, a SET-NAME define, not with a W_* argument token - the only such reuse in the unit.

constellation.doc: Change one named constellation's artwork strength, or the colour of its lines or its label.

name.default: absent or empty -> "command 'constellation': missing name"; a name that matches no constellation changes nothing and only writes "No constellation ... with shortName ..." in the log
name.notes: The value is upper-cased before use (:2519), so `ori` and `Ori` both work. It is NOT evaluated, so $-variables are not substituted.

intensity.doc: How strongly this constellation's artwork is drawn.
intensity.default: absent or empty -> the command goes on to the colour part instead
intensity.notes: When present it wins: the command applies it and returns, so `type`/colour keys on the same line are ignored. `set constellation_art_intensity` does the same for ALL constellations at once.

type.doc: Which part of the constellation the colour is for.

value_docs.line: the lines joining the constellation's stars
value_docs.label: the constellation's name written in the sky

type.default: absent or empty -> "command 'constellation': missing type"; any other value -> "command 'constellation': unknown type"

color_value.doc: The colour, written in one word: either x followed by six hex digits, or the three numbers 0-255 run together after the letters r, g and b.

completable_excluded.xRRGGBB: a SHAPE, not a value: RR/GG/BB stand for two hexadecimal digits each

color_value.default: absent or empty -> the r/g/b keys are used instead

r.default: absent -> 0 when g or b is given; all three absent AND `color_value` absent -> "'color': missing expected argument 'r' or 'g' or 'b'" and the command stops

branches.effect: set that constellation's artwork strength and stop
recolour that constellation's lines or its label

The r/g/b range messages are still lost to the by-value slip recorded in unit 1 (src/interfaceModule/app_command_color.cpp:58-59).
A name that matches no constellation is not an error: the command reports SUCCESS and only the log says nothing was found (src/coreModule/constellation_mgr.cpp:162, :184, :644).

date.doc: Set the date and time the sky is showing, either outright or by moving it along.

jday.doc: The date given as a Julian day -- the running count of days astronomers use, where the whole number changes at noon.
jday.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
jday.notes: The date that lands is kept inside the range the ephemerides can serve (src/coreModule/time_mgr.cpp:45-46). The half-day offset the doc line mentions -- the whole number changing at noon and not at midnight -- is written into the conversion itself (src/appModule/space_date.cpp:239-244).

local.doc: The date and time written out, read as the time on your own clock.
local.value: text of the shape [+/-]YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss -- the T is a letter you write; a value starting with T sets the time only and keeps the day
local.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried; a value that cannot be read -> "Error parsing date local"
local.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3975-3993 -> src/appModule/space_date.cpp:255-279 (reading), 579-594 (the day the T-form keeps) (W_LOCAL="local", base_command_interface.hpp:219)
local.notes: How the text is actually read (src/appModule/space_date.cpp:265): a number, then ONE character of any kind, then the next number, and so on -- so 2020/01/01T00:00:00 is read just as happily as the dashes-and-colons form. A value with no time part is read as that day at 00:00:00. The month must be 1 to 12, the day 1 to 31 (whatever the month), the hour 0 to 23, the minutes and seconds 0 to 59; anything else is refused. The value is then moved by the program's time-zone setting to get the sky's own time (:3988).

utc.doc: The date and time written out, read as universal time (the time at longitude zero) instead of your own.
utc.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried; a value that cannot be read -> "Error parsing date utc"
utc.notes: Same reading as `local` but with no time-zone step, and there is no T-only form here: a value starting with T is refused.

relative.doc: Move the date on by this many days of the body you are standing on -- its own day, which is not always 24 hours.
relative.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
relative.notes: The body's own day is used unless it is longer than 366 of our days, in which case one of our days is used instead (:4017). Standing nowhere -- in the galaxy or the universe view -- the command reports an error (:4012-4015, the message is in French in the source).

relative_year.doc: Move the date on by this many years, keeping the same month, day and time.
relative_year.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
relative_year.notes: The year number is simply added, so a negative value goes back.

relative_month.doc: Move the date on by this many months, keeping the same day and time.
relative_month.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
relative_month.notes: The month number is simply added, so 13 means a year and a month later (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2611).

sidereal.doc: Move the date on by this many turns of the body you are standing on with respect to the stars -- its sidereal day.
sidereal.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
sidereal.notes: Like `relative`, the body's turn is used unless it is longer than 366 of our days (:4048), and standing nowhere gives an error (:4043-4046, French in the source).

load.doc: Take the date from the computer or from the program's own setting.

value_docs.current: set the sky to the computer's date and time right now
value_docs.preset: set the sky to the date the program is configured to start at -- but only when it is configured to start at a preset date, otherwise the computer's date is used (:4063-4065)
value_docs.keep_time: take today's date from the computer but keep the time of day the sky is already showing

load.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried; any other value -> "Command 'date': unknown load value"
load.notes: The setting `preset` reads is the one `set startup_time_mode` writes (families.set_names), and the preset date itself is the configured start date (src/appModule/app.hpp:115-117).

sun.doc: Move the time to one of the Sun's moments of the day where you are standing.

value_docs.set: the time the Sun sets today at your place
value_docs.rise: the time the Sun rises today at your place
value_docs.meridian: the time the Sun is highest today -- local noon
value_docs.midnight: the opposite of local noon: the calculation is made half a world away and the answer moved on one day (:4098-4101)

sun.default: absent or empty -> "command 'date' : unknown argument"; any other value -> nothing happens and the command reports SUCCESS (see `flagged`)
sun.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4084-4105 -> src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:535-547 -> src/coreModule/time_mgr.cpp:62-158 (rise), 159-251 (set), 253-349 (meridian) (W_SUN="sun", W_SET="set", W_RISE="rise", W_MERIDIAN="meridian", W_MIDNIGHT="midnight": base_command_interface.hpp:126, 289, 290, 291, 292)
sun.notes: The calculation uses the longitude and latitude you are at. Where the Sun neither rises nor sets that day, the time goes to about local noon instead (time_mgr.cpp, the |Ho|>1 branch). If the calculation returns exactly zero the date is left alone (:4088, 4092, 4096, 4100 -- each carries the author's own TODO).

branches.selector: the first non-empty of jday, local, utc, relative, relative_year, relative_month, sidereal, load, sun
branches.effect: that one form acts and the command returns; the keys after it are never read
"command 'date' : unknown argument"

notes: The nine forms are tried in a fixed order written into the code (jday, local, utc, relative, relative_year, relative_month, sidereal, load, sun) and only the first one present acts, whatever the order on the line.

Sharp edge on the T-only form of `local`: the day it keeps comes from a text that begins with 'BC ' when the sky is at a year before 1 AD (src/appModule/space_date.cpp:587-593), so the first ten characters are not a date and the command reports 'Error parsing date local'. Only years before 1 AD are affected.

The startup path that this is plainly copied from tests the two spellings 'preset' and 'Preset' (src/appModule/app.cpp:656), and W_PRESET is only "preset" (base_command_interface.hpp:287). So with the setting written 'Preset' the program starts at the preset date but `date load preset` goes to the computer's date instead.

define.doc: Give a name to a value so that later commands can use it instead of writing the number again.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name you choose for the value, the VALUE is what it holds.
key_grammar.key_domain: any word EXCEPT the 24 reserved names (families.reserved_variables): a reserved name is refused with the message "<name> is a reservedVar so you can't define it" written to the program's standard output, and nothing is stored
key_grammar.value: a number, or the name of another variable (its value is copied), or the name of a reserved variable (its current value is copied), or any other text (stored as text, counting as 0 in arithmetic)
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "Unexpected error in command_define" (note that `define x` is no pair: a key with no value is dropped by the parser, parse_model.pair_extraction)

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, and it is the ALPHABETICALLY FIRST key of the line, not the first written: the handler reads args.begin() and never loops (:4649-4651). `define b 2 a 1` defines only `a`. Confirms parse_model.flag_multi_pair's list.

How the value is read (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:143-157): a reserved name gives that reading's current value; an existing variable name gives that variable's value; otherwise the text is converted to a number, and if it is not a number at all it is kept as text with the numeric value 0.
The variables live until the program stops or a script ends (AppCommandInterface::deleteVar, :120-123); `struct print var` lists them.

The map handed downstream therefore differs from the map the line actually wrote -- for these two keys the downstream reads (`find` at dsoNavigator.cpp:264-265, `operator[]` at :321) treat empty and absent alike, so no behaviour changes today; a tool that models 'the keys of this line' must still know the insertion happens.

The four literal key spellings here ("color_tex", "alpha_tex", "depth", "maxobject" at :1680-1688) are written as bare strings, not W_* tokens -- only "maxobject" has a W_* twin (W_MAX_OBJECT, base_command_interface.hpp:100), and the handler does not use it.
flagged: dso3d `z_reflection`: the key is read and discarded (dsoNavigator.cpp:304-306). Whether the intended behaviour should be restored (and what it is) is not answerable from the code -- Vixy. Doc left null.

dso3d `action restart` with `maxobject` present and not '1': std::stoi(args["depth"]) at app_command_interface.cpp:1688 runs on the raw string, and nothing in the call chain catches exceptions (no catch in src/interfaceModule/, src/scriptModule/, src/mainModule/ or src/main.cpp). A missing or non-numeric `depth` therefore aborts the program rather than reporting a script error. Recorded, not fixed (out of scope); the lint rule this suggests needs Vixy's word on severity.

dso3d `pos_x/pos_y/pos_z` unit: the code states no unit for the galaxy-space coordinates (dsoNavigator.cpp:275-277 feeds Mat4f::translation directly). The doc lines say only which direction each moves.

look_at.doc: Turn the view towards a given direction, or nudge it a little from where it points now.

azimuth.doc: Where to look, measured around the horizon in degrees.
azimuth.default: absent or empty -> the turn-to form is not taken (it needs `altitude` as well) and the nudge form is tried instead
azimuth.notes: Degrees: the receiver multiplies by PI/180 (src/navModule/navigator.cpp:149-150).

altitude.doc: Where to look, measured up from the horizon in degrees.
altitude.default: absent or empty -> the turn-to form is not taken and the nudge form is tried instead

duration.doc: How many seconds the turn takes.
duration.default: in the turn-to form, absent -> 1 second (the default argument of CoreLink::lookAt, src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:375); in the nudge form, absent -> 0, i.e. the view jumps at once

delta_azimuth.doc: How far to nudge the view around the horizon -- in RADIANS, not degrees (half a turn is about 3.14).
delta_azimuth.default: absent or empty -> 0, no nudge around; with `delta_altitude` also absent the command reports "Command 'look_at': wrong argument"
delta_azimuth.notes: [derived] Radians: the value is added to an angle that comes out of Utility::rectToSphe, which returns radians (src/tools/utility.cpp:102-107; use at src/navModule/navigator.cpp:186-193) -- no PI/180 anywhere on this path, unlike `azimuth`. It is SUBTRACTED from the current azimuth (src/navModule/navigator.cpp:193), so its sign is the opposite of `azimuth`'s direction.

delta_altitude.doc: How far to nudge the view up or down -- in RADIANS, not degrees (a quarter turn is about 1.57).
delta_altitude.default: absent or empty -> 0, no nudge up or down
delta_altitude.notes: [derived] Radians, same reasoning as `delta_azimuth`. The result is kept between straight down and straight up (src/navModule/navigator.cpp:195-197).

branches.effect: turn the view to that direction over `duration` seconds (1 by default), then return -- the delta keys are never read
nudge the view by those amounts; stops the view following whatever it was following (src/coreModule/core.hpp:266)
"Command 'look_at': wrong argument"

notes: The turn-to form needs BOTH `azimuth` and `altitude`: with only one of them the command falls through to the nudge form and, with no delta key, reports 'wrong argument' -- the given key is silently dropped.

The two forms use different units for the same kind of quantity (degrees for `azimuth`/`altitude`, radians for `delta_azimuth`/`delta_altitude`) and different absent-defaults for `duration` (1 second against 0).

notes: The colour keys, `keycolor` and `speed` are read on the `action play` path only (except `speed`, which has a second reading of its own at :3917): the see-through colour of a video that is already playing cannot be changed.
Colour errors are deliberately swallowed here: when the colour helper reports one, the message is thrown away (:3879-3880) and the video plays unchanged.

C1-relevant, the audio-only path (:3676): the handler calls executeCommand again from inside itself, and that call CLEARS and refills `args` and replaces `commandline` (:332-335). Two consequences: nothing after :3676 may read `args` (nothing does -- the call is returned immediately), and a recording of `media action play audioname x` stores the rebuilt `audio ...` line instead of the line the author wrote (executeCommandStatus :1311).

Also C1-relevant at :3676: the rebuilt line ends with 'loop ' when `loop` is absent -- a key with no value, which the parser silently drops (parse_model.pair_extraction). And an audio file name containing spaces cannot survive the rebuild, because the quotes were already stripped when the line was parsed.
`action play` needs the video file to exist even when `type` is image: the picture is a video texture (:3691-3695, src/mediaModule/media.cpp:219-222).
The five actions each return at once, so no line can both play and stop.
flagged: media `subtitle` on its own (app_command_interface.cpp:3927-3936): the toggle test at :3929 reads `argAction`, not `argSubtitle`. `media subtitle toggle` therefore does NOT flip the subtitles -- 'toggle' is not an on-form, so it HIDES them -- while `media action toggle subtitle <anything>` flips them. The `action play` reading of the same key (:3778) does it correctly. Which of the two is the intended spelling decides what the editor documents and completes: Vixy. Recorded, not fixed (out of scope).

media `speed` / `speed_increment`: FixedPointI16_2::fromString throws on any character that is not a figure, a sign or a point, and on more than one point (src/tools/fixed_point.hpp:397-421, with THROW_ON_FIXED_POINT_ERROR = 1 at src/tools/fixed_point.hpp:12); nothing in the call chain catches it (same check as for timerate). `media speed fast`, or `media speed $var`, therefore stops the program. Same class as the unit-1 dso3d `depth` finding; lint severity needs Vixy. Recorded, not fixed.
