latitude.doc: The same thing as `lat`, spelled out.
latitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or default / inverse
latitude.default: absent or empty -> the latitude you are at now is kept
latitude.notes: Read only when `lat` is empty (:3572), so `lat` wins when both are on the line.

lon.doc: Where to go: how far east (a positive number) or west (a negative one), in degrees.
lon.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or one of the two words below

value_docs.default: the longitude the program starts at (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:888-890)
value_docs.inverse: half a turn round the body: the present longitude plus 180 degrees

lon.default: absent or empty -> `longitude` is read instead; if that is empty too, the longitude you are at now is kept

longitude.doc: The same thing as `lon`, spelled out.
longitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or default / inverse
longitude.default: absent or empty -> the longitude you are at now is kept

alt.doc: How high to stand above the body, in metres; a value that starts with + or - is added to your present height instead of replacing it.
alt.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or the word default

value_docs.default: the height the program starts at (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:892-894)

alt.default: absent or empty -> `altitude` is read instead; if that is empty too, the height you are at now is kept
alt.notes: The word `inverse` is NOT accepted here, unlike `lat` and `lon`. The + / - test looks at the first character of the text (:3603), so it is the written sign that matters, not the value: `alt +0` is relative, `alt 5` is not.

altitude.doc: The same thing as `alt`, spelled out.
altitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or default, or a value starting with + or -
altitude.default: absent or empty -> the height you are at now is kept

delta_lat.doc: How many degrees to move north (positive) or south (negative) from where the move already puts you.

delta_lon.doc: How many degrees to move east (positive) or west (negative) from where the move already puts you.

delta_alt.doc: How many metres to rise (positive) or drop (negative) from the height the move already puts you at.

multiply_alt.doc: Multiply the height by this number -- 2 puts you twice as high, 0.5 half as high.
multiply_alt.notes: Applied AFTER `delta_alt` (:3616-3621), so the two compose in that order whatever the order on the line.

duration.doc: How many seconds the move takes; leave it out to arrive at once.
duration.default_value_source: app_command_interface.cpp:3623 (unguarded args[] lookup) -> app_command_eval.cpp:116-133 -> src/tools/utility.cpp:399-406 (strToDouble catches and returns default_value 0, utility.hpp:143)
duration.notes: Turned into whole milliseconds (:3623), so anything under a thousandth of a second is the same as 0.

branches.selector: at least one of lat/latitude, lon/longitude, alt/altitude, delta_lat, delta_lon, delta_alt, multiply_alt
branches.effect: work out the target place from the present one, then move there over `duration`
"command 'move_to' : missing lat && lon && alt"

notes: The target is built in a fixed order: start from where you are now, replace with `lat`/`lon`/`alt` if given, then add the delta keys, then multiply the height (:3581-3621). The order written on the line never matters.
The emptiness test at :3577 counts the SHORT spellings only after they have absorbed the long ones (:3572-3574), so `moveto latitude 45` is enough on its own.

The place the move starts from is the place the drawn path reports, which is not always the one the old observer holds (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:836-852): after a `camera action descend`, `delta_alt` and `multiply_alt` compute from the camera's height.

What lands is clamped differently on the two paths: the old observer holds latitude within +/-90 degrees and never goes below 0.1 metre of height (src/navModule/observer.cpp:61-64), the camera clamps nothing (recorded in src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:850-852, not a thing this command decides).
The error text spells the command 'move_to' though the command is `moveto` (:3578).

multiply.doc: Multiply a named value by a number.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is what to multiply it by.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__multiply"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4690-4692). Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.

divide.doc: Divide a named value by a number.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is what to divide it by.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__divide"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4703-4705). Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.
Nothing checks for a zero divisor: the division is plain floating-point, so dividing by 0 stores an infinite value (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:10).

modulo.doc: Replace a named value by what is left over after dividing it by a number.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is the number to divide by.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__modulo"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4716-4718). The remainder is the floating-point one (std::fmod), so it works with values that are not whole numbers. Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.

tangent.doc: Put the tangent of an angle into a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name that RECEIVES the result, the VALUE is the angle in degrees.
key_grammar.key_domain: as `add` -- but note the name's current value is not used at all, it is overwritten
key_grammar.value: number of degrees, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__tangent"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4729-4731).

Unlike add/sub/multiply/divide/modulo this is NOT a two-sided operation: the function ignores the variable's current value and stores the tangent of the value written (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:12). The angle is in degrees, converted with 3.1415926 (a shortened value of pi, so results carry a small error).

trunc.doc: Put a number, with everything after its decimal point cut off, into a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name that RECEIVES the result, the VALUE is the number to cut.
key_grammar.key_domain: as `add` -- the name's current value is not used, it is overwritten
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__trunc"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4742-4744). Cutting is towards zero: -2.7 becomes -2.

sinus.doc: Put the sine of an angle into a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name that RECEIVES the result, the VALUE is the angle in degrees.
key_grammar.key_domain: as `add` -- the name's current value is not used, it is overwritten
key_grammar.value: number of degrees, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__sinus"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4755-4757). Degrees, converted with the same shortened pi as `tangent`.

personal.doc: Draw your own set of lines on the sky, placed in the observer's own frame - the one the horizon is fixed in.

action.doc: Whether to load a drawing from a file or erase the one being drawn.

value_docs.load: read the points from a file and draw them

action.default: absent -> the command looks for `xy` instead; present with any other value -> "command_personal: Unknown 'action' value"

filename.doc: The file holding the points to draw.
filename.notes: A name that is not an absolute path is taken relative to the script folder (CallSystem::isAbsolute + scriptInterface->getScriptPath(), :1578-1579). xy.doc: The points to draw given directly on the command line instead of in a file.
xy.value: string -- numbers separated by ';', read in pairs
xy.default: absent (and no `action`) -> "command_'personal' : unrecognized or malformed argument"
xy.notes: Each pair is an angle around then an angle up, used as-is (radians -- the file form's degree conversion is NOT applied here): src/coreModule/skyDisplay.cpp:308-337 with Utility::spheToRect(lng, lat) (src/tools/utility.hpp:135-137). An odd count drops the last number and logs 'Skyperson loading incomplete data' (skyDisplay.cpp:322-325).

branches.effect: load from file / clear; returns before `xy` is ever looked at
draw the points given inline

notes: 'held in the observer's own frame' is the code's SkyDisplay::AL projection: the drawing is placed with the local-to-eye matrix (src/coreModule/skydisplay_mgr.cpp:176-179 creates SKY_PERSONAL as SkyPerson(SkyDisplay::AL); src/coreModule/skyDisplay.cpp:226 chooses getMatLocalToEye for AL). `personeq` is the same drawing in the sky's frame.
The colour of this drawing is set by 'color property personal' (families.color_names).

personeq.doc: Draw your own set of lines on the sky, placed in the sky's frame - the one the stars are fixed in, so the lines follow them.

action.doc: Whether to load a drawing from a file or erase the one being drawn.

value_docs.load: read the points from a file and draw them

action.default: absent -> the command looks for `xy` instead; present with any other value -> "command_personeq: Unknown 'action' value"

filename.doc: The file holding the points to draw.
filename.notes: A name that is not an absolute path is taken relative to the script folder (:1727-1728). Same file shape as `personal` (src/coreModule/skyDisplay.cpp:249-271).

xy.doc: The points to draw given directly on the command line instead of in a file.
xy.value: string -- numbers separated by ';', read in pairs
xy.default: absent (and no `action`) -> "command_'personeq' : unrecognized or malformed argument"
xy.notes: Same reading as `personal.xy` (src/coreModule/skyDisplay.cpp:308-337): pairs of angles used as-is, an odd count drops the last number with a log line.

branches.effect: load from file / clear; returns before `xy` is looked at
draw the points given inline

notes: 'held in the sky's own frame' is the code's SkyDisplay::EQ projection: the drawing is placed with the equatorial-to-eye matrix (src/coreModule/skydisplay_mgr.cpp:183-186 creates SKY_PERSONEQ as SkyPerson(SkyDisplay::EQ); src/coreModule/skyDisplay.cpp:226).
Byte-for-byte the same handler shape as `personal` with the other target and the other default file name.

planet_scale.doc: Draw one solar-system body larger or smaller than its true size.

name.default: absent or empty -> "command 'planet_scale' : missing name or scale argument", nothing changes

scale.doc: How many times its true size to draw it at.
scale.default: absent or empty -> same error as a missing name; nothing changes

notes: Both keys are tested together (`!argName.empty() && !argScale.empty()`), so the one error message covers either omission (:1516-1519).
The value is read as a string first and only then evaluated, so `scale` is never absent-defaulted to 0 here: an empty value takes the error path instead.

position.doc: Remember where and when you are, in one single bookmark, or go back to what was remembered.

action.doc: Whether to record the present view or to return to the recorded one.

value_docs.save: record the date, the field of view, the place you are looking from, the body you are on and which scale you are in
value_docs.load: go back to what was recorded

action.default: absent or any other value -> "Command 'position': unknown parameter"

notes: One bookmark only, held in memory and lost when the program stops: date, field of view, latitude, longitude, altitude, home body, current scale (src/coreModule/backup_mgr.hpp:45-56). This is NOT the `session` command, which writes a file.

`load` before any `save` skips the place-and-date part (the recorded date is 0, src/coreModule/backup_mgr.cpp:49) but still runs the last two lines: it asks for an empty body name and puts you back in the solar-system scale (src/coreModule/backup_mgr.cpp:75-76, the struct's defaults).
The place is read from, and restored to, the path that actually draws (src/coreModule/backup_mgr.cpp:59-73, 82-90) -- the same seam `moveto` uses.

print.doc: Write text into the program's log: one line per key given, showing the key and its value.

key_grammar.doc: Any key you like, with the text to write as its value; each pair becomes one log line '[key] text'.
key_grammar.key_domain: unrestricted -- this is the only command in the unit that accepts keys from no list
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> "command_'print': malformed command" (note that `print hello` is no pair: a key with no value is dropped by the parser, parse_model.pair_extraction)

notes: The pairs are written in ALPHABETICAL order of key, not the order they appear on the line (`args` is a std::map, src/tools/utility.hpp:85; iteration at :2138). C1-relevant: a tool that echoes a print line must not promise the written order.
Each pair is written twice: once into the script log file and once into the general log, both at warning level (:2142-2143).

The declared handler range 1969-2109 (next handler at :2273) contains, after the handler body ends at :2146, the unrelated member AppCommandInterface::readValue (:2156-2271). No `args[` occurrence lives there; the count gate is unaffected.

random.doc: Set the range that the built-in chance value is drawn from.

min.doc: The smallest number the chance value may take.

max.doc: The largest number the chance value may take.

branches.effect: set one or both ends of the range; both may be given on one line
debug_message "unknown random parameter"

notes: This is the one command of the unit that reads TWO keys of its own and acts on both: at least one of them must be there.

The range is used by the reserved name `random` (families.reserved_variables), which gives a new evenly-drawn number between the two ends every time it is read (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:338-339). Nothing checks that min is below max.

script.wait_parameter: commandScript(uint64_t &wait): `script action pause` sets wait = 1, which makes the caller hold before the next line (app_command_interface.cpp:2990-2992)
script.doc: Start, stop, pause or speed up a script, or record what is being done into a new script.

action.doc: What to do.

value_docs.end: stop the running script and clear what it put on screen: texts, music and every non-permanent picture
value_docs.record: start writing every command that follows into the file named by `filename`
value_docs.cancelrecord: stop recording and throw the recording away
value_docs.pause: hold the running script where it is
value_docs.resume: let a held script go on
value_docs.default: run the script at its normal speed
value_docs.acquire: take the global lock (only with `lock global`)
value_docs.release: give the global lock back (only with `lock global`)

action.default: absent -> `speed` is used instead; both absent -> "command_'script' : missing action argument"; an unknown value -> "command_script : unknown parameter from 'action' argument"
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:2962, 2966-3011 (W_ACTION="action" base_command_interface.hpp:81; W_END="end" :157, W_PLAY="play" :158, W_RECORD="record" :84, W_CANCEL="cancelrecord" :159, W_PAUSE="pause" :160, W_RESUME="resume" :168, W_FASTER="faster" :161, W_SLOWER="slower" :162, W_DEFAULT="default" :143, W_ACQUIRE="acquire" :322, W_RELEASE="release" :323)

filename.doc: The script file to play, or the file to record into.
filename.default: absent or empty with `action play` -> the line falls through to "command_script : unknown parameter from 'action' argument"
filename.notes: Sharp edge: the name is treated as a VARIABLE and evaluated only when it does NOT look like it already has a three-letter extension - the test is 'shorter than 4 characters, or the fourth character from the end is not a dot' (:2964-2965). On `action play` the file is looked for in the script folder and the folder it is found in becomes the script path used by later commands (:2977-2982).

lock.doc: Takes or gives back the lock that keeps two scripts from running at once.

value_docs.global: the one lock shared by every script

lock.default: absent or any other value with `action acquire`/`action release` -> nothing happens and the command still reports SUCCESS
lock.notes: Only read on the `acquire` and `release` paths (:3001-3008); on every other action it is ignored.

speed.doc: Change how fast the running script goes, without an `action`.
speed.default: absent -> `action` must be given instead; an unknown value -> "command_script : unknown parameter from 'speed' argument"
speed.notes: Only read when no `action` is written: the action block always returns (:3011).

notes: `action record` and `action cancelrecord` set recordable = 0 (:2986, :2989) so the command itself never appears in the file being recorded.
`action pause` on a script that is ALREADY paused, or when skip-pause is on, falls into the pause-or-resume branch and RESUMES it instead (:2990-2994).
The comment at :3024-3029 records why the `speed` branch returns: without it a working `script speed ...` reported failure and was dropped from every recorded show (INTENT S11.108 rider).
This is one of the three commands in the sweep that take the `wait` parameter (with `wait` and `zoom` in units 1 and 3).

search.doc: Look for objects whose name starts with a given text and send the list of matches back over the network connection.

name.doc: The beginning of the name to look for.
name.default: absent or empty -> "command 'search' : missing name argument", nothing is searched

maxobject.doc: How many matches to send back at most.
maxobject.default: absent -> 5 (the default argument of Core::getListMatchingObjects, src/coreModule/core.hpp:345)
maxobject.default_value_source: app_command_interface.cpp:1497-1500 (empty takes the one-argument overload) -> src/coreModule/core.hpp:345 (`unsigned int maxNbItem=5`)

notes: The reply is the matching names joined by ';' (src/coreModule/core.cpp:207-216); when nothing matched the literal 'NOF' is sent instead (:1502-1503).
With no network connection the search still runs and the result is discarded (`if (tcp)`, :1504-1505) -- the command reports success either way.

session.note: B31 session save/load; explicit-only by design (D33)
session.doc: Save or load a named session preset: the observed universe and the operator's settings.

action.doc: Whether to write the current state to a session file or read one back.

value_docs.save: Write the current state into the named session file.
value_docs.load: Read a named session file back and apply it.

action.default: absent or any other value -> "Command 'session': unknown or missing action, expected 'save' or 'load'", nothing happens

filename.doc: The name to save under or load from; leave it out to use the one default session.
filename.notes: It is a NAME, not a path: the file is written as sessions/<name> with '.ini' appended when the name contains no dot; a name containing '/' or '\' is refused with an explanatory log line and nothing is written or loaded (SessionFile.cpp:45-57, DIRECTORY = "sessions" SessionFile.hpp:211). The handler's own comment states the optionality on both save and load (:1475-1477).

notes: Failure of the underlying save/load is reported as "Command 'session': the session could not be saved/loaded" (:1481, :1484); the detailed reason is in the log, not in the command result.

select.doc: Choose the object the program points at and describes -- a star, a body of the solar system, a deep-sky object or a constellation.

hp.doc: The number of a star in the Hipparcos star catalogue.
hp.value: int (read with std::istringstream in the receiver, not evaluated here)
hp.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
hp.notes: A number no star answers to selects nothing and reports success (Core::selectObject returns 0, src/coreModule/core.cpp:1133-1158).

star.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried

planet.doc: The name of a body of the solar system; the word home_planet means the body you are standing on.

value_docs.home_planet: whatever body you are standing on right now (its English name is looked up and used instead, app_command_interface.cpp:3282-3283)

planet.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
planet.notes: Names are matched against both body trees, the old one first (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1092-1097).

body.doc: Another spelling of `planet`: the name of a body of the solar system.
body.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
body.notes: Handled exactly like `planet` (the same select_type W_PLANET is used, :3285), so the two spellings differ only in which is tried first: `planet` wins when both are on the line.

nebula.doc: The name of a deep-sky object (a galaxy, a nebula or a cluster).
nebula.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried

constellation.doc: The short name of a constellation to select, or the word zodiac to select the twelve constellations of the zodiac at once.
constellation.value: string (a constellation short name), or the word zodiac

value_docs.zodiac: select the twelve zodiac constellations together: Ari, Tau, Gem, Cnc, Leo, Vir, Sco, Sgr, Cap, Aqr, Psc, Lib (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1169-1186)

constellation.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
constellation.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3268-3271 (zodiac) and 3127-3129 (one constellation) -> src/coreModule/core.cpp:1104-1110 (W_CONSTELLATION="constellation", base_command_interface.hpp:97; W_ZODIAC="zodiac", base_command_interface.hpp:274)
constellation.notes: The short name is matched without regard to case (src/coreModule/constellation_mgr.cpp findFromAbbreviation uppercases both sides). Selecting a constellation clears the selected OBJECT (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1109-1110), so nothing is described afterwards.

constellation_star.doc: The short name of a constellation whose brightest star should be selected -- the way to centre the view on a constellation.
constellation_star.default: absent or empty -> nothing is selected: "command 'select' : no object found"

pointer.doc: Say off to select the object without drawing the marker around it.
values: off-forms per Utility::isFalse ("0", "off", "false", case-insensitive; src/tools/utility.hpp:172-183) = no marker
anything else, and absent = the marker is drawn
pointer.default: absent -> the marker is turned ON (isFalse("") is false, so the else branch runs)
pointer.notes: Read AFTER the object has been chosen, and only on the path that chose one: the `constellation zodiac` form returns at :3270 and the no-object form at :3300, so `pointer` does nothing on either. It has the last word over the marker handling inside the selection code (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2369, 2374).

branches.effect: select the twelve zodiac constellations and return; `pointer` is not read

branches.selector: first non-empty of hp, star, planet, body, nebula, constellation, constellation_star
branches.effect: select that object, then show or hide the marker

branches.selector: none of the seven identity keys
branches.effect: "command 'select' : no object found"

notes: The seven identity keys are tried in a FIXED order written into the code -- hp, star, planet, body, nebula, constellation, constellation_star (:3273-3297) -- and the first one present wins, whatever order the author wrote them in. The zodiac test comes before all of them (:3268).
Selecting something stops the view from following what it was following (Core::selectObject sets tracking off, src/coreModule/core.cpp:1133-1156).

set.doc: Give one or more named settings a new value.

args._see: families.set_names -- the 43 names, with their per-name value domain, default, doc and source. Written once, there (I2); this object holds no key entry on purpose. See args_source below.

key_grammar.doc: Each pair is the NAME of a setting and the VALUE to give it; several pairs may be written on one line.
key_grammar.key_domain: families.set_names - the 43 registered names (app_command_init.cpp:302-345 x base_command_interface.hpp:551-594); an unregistered name gives "command_'set': unknown argument" plus a nearest-name suggestion in the log, and that pair does nothing
key_grammar.value: depends on the name - see args
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> "command_'set': malformed command", nothing changes
key_grammar.source: app_command_interface.cpp:2276-2286 (loop), :2306-2395 (per-name effects), :2290-2303 (name lookup); name table app_command_init.cpp:302-345

set.args_source: families.set_names - the 43 names ARE this command's argument keys, and their per-name value domain, default, doc and source live there in the D7 v2 object shape. Written once (I2): this `args` stays empty on purpose, and the family-name half of `unknown-parameter` is what reports an unknown key of `set`.
notes: MULTI-PAIR, unlike `flag`: commandSet loops over EVERY pair (:2282-2285). The pairs act in ALPHABETICAL key order (args is a std::map), not in the order written - `set star_scale 2 home_planet Mars` applies home_planet first.
The line's result is the AND of every pair (:2284): one unknown name makes the whole line report failure.

C1/recorder sharp edge: debug_message is cleared once per LINE (executeCommand :330) but evalCommandSet ends EVERY pair with executeCommandStatus() (:2394). (a) Once one pair fails, every later pair of the same line also reports failure. (b) While recording, a line of N good pairs writes the WHOLE line N times into the recorded script (executeCommandStatus :1311 records `commandline`).
The did-you-mean on an unknown name is computed from args.begin()->first (:2388) - the alphabetically first key of the line, not the name that failed.
parseCommandSet (:2290-2303) is a linear scan over the 43-name map; its only `args[` occurrence (:2294) is commented out.
Two set names duplicate a command of the same name with different reach: `set heading` (no duration) vs the `heading` command, and `set screen_fader` vs the `screen_fader` command.
flagged: set `mode`: registered, parses, reports success, does nothing (`case APP_MODE: break;` :2392). What it was meant to do - and therefore its value domain and doc line - is not answerable from the code. Vixy.

set `datetime_display_position`: the number is a screen coordinate whose meaning (units, origin, allowed values) the code never states; src/uiModule/ui_tuiconf.cpp:106/:112 only take it modulo 120 or 180. Doc line says what the setting is for, not what a given number does. Vixy (or a uiModule extraction pass).
set `datetime_display_number`: the accepted numbers are decided by the switch at src/uiModule/ui_tuiconf.cpp:104, outside this unit's range; the value domain is recorded as int only.
set `line_width`, `star_mag_scale`, `moon_brightness`, `sun_brightness`: the code states no unit and no allowed range for any of them. Recorded as plain numbers.

action.doc: Confirms that the program really should close.
action.default: absent, empty or any other value -> "Bad shutdown request." and nothing happens

notes: The only working line is `shutdown action now`; there is no confirmation and no saving.
It sets the application's ALIVE flag to false (:2400), which ends the main loop.

sky_culture.doc: Load a different set of constellations and star names (a sky culture) from a folder.

path.doc: The folder holding the sky culture's files.
path.default: absent or empty -> "command_sky_culture : path or action missing"
path.notes: Sharp edge: the path is resolved as though it were a PICTURE file (FilePath TFP::IMAGE, :2951), so a bare name is looked for in the script folder first and then in the picture folder, and the result is used even when nothing exists there - existence is never checked (src/tools/file_path.cpp:102-145). The folder is expected to contain constellation_names.eng.fab and star_names.fab (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1550, :1563).

action.doc: The one action this command knows.

value_docs.load: read the culture from that folder and use it

notes: RECONCILIATION with parse_model.pre_table_commands (the unit-4 assignment). `struct` IS both intercepted before the table (:357-358) and registered (app_command_init.cpp:90) -- but the two paths are not equivalent: (a) the interception happens BEFORE the skip test at :245, which is why a `struct` line still runs inside a switched-off or skipped block -- without that, no `struct if end` could ever close a block it is inside; (b) the REGISTERED path is dead code: the switch case for SC_STRUCT is an empty `break;` labelled '// for g++ warning' (:443), so reaching the table with the command `struct` would do nothing -- and it cannot be reached anyway, since the literal test at :357 already caught it. What the registration actually buys is presence in the did-you-mean list and in the enum-to-name map used by the recorder (app_command_init.cpp:111-127). REFINES the parse_model line, which today says only 'struct is also registered'.

The `if` branch is guarded by `swapCommand != true` (:4770): inside a block switched off by `comment` (or by `struct comment true`), conditional lines are ignored -- but `struct comment false` still works, since the `comment` branch has no such guard. This is what makes a switched-off block closable.

The `if` branch is NOT guarded by the if-skip state, which is what makes nesting work: every `struct if` inside a skipped block still pushes a level, so its own `end` pops the right one (src/interfaceModule/if_swap.cpp:57-62, 90-99).
A block is skipped when ANY enclosing level says skip (src/interfaceModule/if_swap.cpp:90-99), so a false outer condition cannot be undone by a true inner one.
The `loop` branch does NOT return when the count is exactly 1, so such a line falls through to the `print` test (:4871-4878) -- the only path in the handler where two branches can act on one line.

center.default: absent, or any other value -> "Command 'zoom': unknown argument"
center.notes: Compared against the exact text 'on': '1', 'true', 'ON' and 'On' do NOT work here, unlike the on/off grammar used by `flag` and by `manual` just above. The view moves over the application's own move duration, while the SCRIPT waits `duration` seconds (5 by default).

branches.effect: zoom in on / out from the selected object
move the width of view to that many degrees

branches.selector: auto and fov absent, delta_fov non-empty
branches.effect: change the width of view at once
centre the selected object and hold the SCRIPT for `duration` seconds
"Command 'zoom': unknown argument"

notes: One form per line, in the fixed order auto, fov, delta_fov, center.

The `center` form is the only one that holds the script: `wait` is set to duration x 1000 milliseconds (:3461) and only when that is more than 0. Every other form returns at once while the view keeps moving on its own.
The `auto` form reads `duration` twice -- once as a positive number for every branch (:3435) and once as an emptiness test for the default (:3441).

comment.registration: NOT in m_commands: literal string compare before the table lookup (app_command_interface.cpp:351-352). Confirms parse_model.pre_table_commands.
comment.doc: Start a skipped block: the lines after this one are read but not carried out, until an 'uncomment' line.

key_grammar.doc: This command takes no key. Anything written after it is parsed as key/value pairs and ignored.
key_grammar.key_domain: none -- the handler reads no key

notes: The whole handler is `swapCommand = true` (:3327), the flag the executor tests before dispatching anything: while it is set, every command is skipped and logged 'this command has not been executed' (executeCommand :361-364, field declared app_command_interface.hpp:214).

Because `comment`, `uncomment` and `struct` are compared BEFORE the skip test (:351-358 vs :361), those three still act inside a skipped block -- which is what makes the block closable at all. A second `comment` inside a block changes nothing.

The skip state belongs to the interface, not to the file: it is cleared at construction (:73) and by `script action end` (:2972, unit 2), and reaching the end of a script runs exactly that (terminateScript :291-302 <- src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:347). So a block left open at the end of a script does not leak into the next one.
Being outside m_commands also means the did-you-mean suggester can never propose these two names (parse_model.pre_table_commands).
There is one more `unskippable` escape: `terminateScript` sets it (:301) so the closing `script action end` runs even inside a skipped block (:361).

uncomment.registration: NOT in m_commands: literal string compare before the table lookup (app_command_interface.cpp:354-355). Confirms parse_model.pre_table_commands.
uncomment.doc: End a block started by 'comment': the lines after this one are carried out again.

key_grammar.doc: This command takes no key. Anything written after it is parsed as key/value pairs and ignored.
key_grammar.key_domain: none -- the handler reads no key

notes: The whole handler is `swapCommand = false` (:3334). An 'uncomment' with no 'comment' before it is legal and does nothing.
It does NOT close the other skip state: `struct if`'s own flag (ifSwap) is tested in the same condition (:361) and is cleared by its own commands, not by this one.

names.notes: IMPORTANT and easy to get wrong: this writes a STATIC DEFAULT, not the colour of anything already on screen. names.name: star_table
names.doc: The colour used for stars of one shade; index picks the shade, 0 for the bluest through 127 for the reddest.
names.source: registration app_command_init.cpp:286, spelling base_command_interface.hpp:546, case app_command_interface.cpp:1871 (the only case that passes index) -> coreLink.cpp:667-669 -> HipStarMgr::setColorStarTable hip_star_mgr.cpp:131-138, writing the static color_table[128] declared hip_star_mgr.cpp:104; every star is drawn with color_table[its own shade index] at zone_array.cpp:293 and :382 and hip_star_wrapper.hpp:93
names.notes: WHAT THE INDEX SELECTS: one of the 128 slots of the star colour table, keyed on the star's colour index. Slot i stands for B-V = i*(4/127) - 0.5 (IndexToBV, hip_star.hpp:46-49), so slot 0 is B-V -0.5 (hottest, blue) and slot 127 is B-V +3.5 (coolest, red). The slots are filled at startup from the 'colors' section of stars.ini, keys color_000 to color_127 (hip_star_mgr.cpp:112-129). An index outside 0-127 changes nothing and logs 'ColorTable index Error' (hip_star_mgr.cpp:133-135). An omitted index means slot 0, because evalInt of an absent key returns 0 (app_command_interface.cpp:2050 and :4641-4642) - so `color property star_table value 1,0,0` silently repaints the bluest stars red. This is the only colour with no getter at any level (app_command_interface.cpp:1877-1880).

names.name: lunar_eclipse_umbra
names.doc: Meant for the ring of Earth's deep shadow at the Moon's distance, but nothing is drawn, so this has no effect.

names.notes: DEAD AT THIS HEAD. Core builds exactly twenty sky lines at core.cpp:128-149 and neither eclipse type is among them; a search of src/ finds no other skyLineMgr->Create call site. So SkyLineMgr::setColor walks an empty match, logs 'SkyLineMgr error : setColor not found LINE_LUNAR_ECLIPSE_UMBRA' at skyline_mgr.cpp:153 and returns. The script sees success. The matching flag `flag lunar_eclipse_umbra on` is equally inert. Worse for a saved session: the read side, SkyLineMgr::getColor, returns the fallback baseColor for a missing line (skyline_mgr.cpp:164-165) rather than failing, so a session would record a colour that was never anyone's.

_acceptance_test.source: src/appModule/fontFactory.cpp:141-169 (lookup at :149-153); the accepted set is the std::map m_strToTarget filled in FontFactory::setStrToTarget, src/appModule/fontFactory.cpp:41-53
_acceptance_test.case_sensitive_evidence: fontFactory.cpp:149 is m_strToTarget.find(targetName) on a std::map<std::string, CLASSEFONT> (declared fontFactory.hpp:115) with the default std::less<std::string>, i.e. a plain byte comparison. Neither commandFont (app_command_interface.cpp:4314-4349) nor updateFont applies any case folding to the target, unlike the `size` and `align` keys of the `text` command which are explicitly upper-cased (app_command_interface.cpp:2861, 2864). So "Text" or "STARS" are rejected.
_acceptance_test.on_unknown: Silent-to-the-script no-op with a log line: fontFactory.cpp:150-153 writes "Unknown FontFactory target " + targetName at LOG_TYPE::L_WARNING (fontFactory.cpp:151) and returns. No exception, no assert, no abort. updateFont returns void and commandFont does not test anything after calling it (app_command_interface.cpp:4338-4340), so debug_message stays empty and the `font` command reports SUCCESS to the script for a misspelt target. A wrong target name is therefore invisible in the script and visible only in the engine log.
_acceptance_test.differs_from_TF_list: no - the accepted set is EXACTLY the ten TF_* spellings. setStrToTarget (fontFactory.cpp:43-52) inserts exactly the ten macros TF_TEXT, TF_PLANETS, TF_CONSTELLATIONS, TF_CARDINAL, TF_STARS, TF_MENU, TF_NEBULAE, TF_GRIDS, TF_LINES, TF_DISPLAYS (base_command_interface.hpp:684-693), one entry each, and setStrToTarget is the only writer of m_strToTarget (it is called only from the constructor, fontFactory.cpp:38). The family check for `font` can be armed as a closed, case-sensitive, exactly-ten-member set.
_acceptance_test.cross_check: core.cpp:1594-1603 calls updateFont with nine literal targets (text, menu, planets, constellations, cardinal_points, grids, lines, displays, stars) at every sky-locale change; the tenth, "nebulae", is at core.cpp:1603. All ten literals are in the accepted set, and no literal outside the TF_* list appears.
notes: Naming inversion worth knowing: TF_TEXT ("text") maps to CLASSEFONT::CLASS_MENU and TF_MENU ("menu") maps to CLASSEFONT::CLASS_UI (fontFactory.cpp:43 and :48). CLASS_MENU is the Media/TextMgr font, not a menu font. Reading the enumerator name instead of the map will give the wrong answer for both targets.

CLASS_MENU is the only accepted target that is not in listFont: it is special-cased and returns early at fontFactory.cpp:156-159 via media->updateTextFont. The other nine are pushed into listFont by FontFactory::init (fontFactory.cpp:91-131).

The assert(0) at fontFactory.cpp:167 fires only if an accepted target resolves to a CLASSEFONT absent from listFont; after a normal init() that cannot happen for any of the ten, so it is dead code on the `font` command path.
The `font` command surface also has the target-free form `font action initial`, which rebuilds every font at its startup size and name (fontFactory.cpp:202-206) and never consults the accepted set.

lint_seeds.rule: unknown command name. The engine logs a Levenshtein nearest neighbour with NO distance threshold (searchNeighbour); scedit reproduces that engine behaviour in its library and CAPS ONLY THE DISPLAY: a suggestion is printed when its distance is at most TWO edits, or one edit per three characters of the misspelt token, whichever is more permissive. See util/scedit/tests/derivation-diff.md S5.7.

unknown flag/set/color name for its subfamily, OR a key that is not an argument of the command. The second half is armed per command by the presence of `args` data AND `args_complete: true`; a command whose entry says args_complete:false is silent on its keys by construction.

lint_seeds.rule: obsolete token (7 names) -- engine silently no-ops with a debug log
'flag sky_draw' -- name spelled in the header but never registered; engine treats it as unknown
odd token count after command -- engine silently drops the trailing key
duplicate key in one line -- engine keeps the LAST value silently

multiple pairs on one of the ten single-pair commands (flag + define/add/sub/multiply/divide/modulo/tangent/trunc/sinus): the engine applies only the alphabetically-first pair. `set` is NOT one of them - see parse_model.set_multi_pair.
flag value not in {on-forms, off-forms, toggle}: engine reads it as OFF silently
single quotes or backslash escapes: the engine parser has neither (sts-extension currently highlights both as if legal)
'set mode' parses and reports success but does nothing engine-side

a byte that LOOKS like a space but is not one to the engine (0xA0 first: the ISO-8859 no-break space; also the UTF-8 encodings of U+00A0, U+2000-U+200B, U+202F, U+3000 and the U+FEFF byte-order mark), sitting outside a quoted value on a line the engine parses. The parser's whitespace set is the C locale's (SP TAB LF VT FF CR), so such a byte does not separate: it joins the words on either side of it into ONE token, and every pair after that point shifts by one.

lint_seeds.co_fires: YES, deliberately: this rule names the CAUSE and the consequence rules (dangling-key / unknown-command / unknown-parameter) still name what the engine will DO. Both are true and separately actionable, and suppressing a true finding because another rule explains it would make the finding set depend on rule order. The cause is emitted FIRST on the line.
